The most suspicious buggy method is:

`com.google.javascript.jscomp.NameAnalyzer.FindReferences.visit(com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeTraversal, com.google.javascript.rhino.Node, com.google.javascript.rhino.Node)`

Why:
- The failure is specific to `goog.inherits(...)` in smart name removal / `NameAnalyzer`.
- Static analysis shows that for class-defining calls, `createNameInformation(...)` recognizes `goog.inherits(SubClass, SuperClass)` and returns:
  - `nameInfo.name = subclassName`
  - `nameInfo.superclass = superclassName`
  - `nameInfo.onlyAffectsClassDef = true`
- Then `FindReferences.visit(...)` does two things:
  1. records the inheritance edge from subclass to superclass
  2. also records a regular reference from subclass to the helper function name itself (`goog.inherits`)

That second edge is here:

- line 842-843:
  `recordReference(nameInfo.name, nodeName, RefType.REGULAR);`

For the failing test, `nodeName` is `goog.inherits`.

This is highly suspicious because:
- the subclass `ns.PageSelectionModel.ChangeEvent` is otherwise unreferenced
- yet the output preserves:
  `goog.inherits(ns.PageSelectionModel.ChangeEvent,ns.PageSelectionModel.FooEvent)`
- preserving only the helper call is exactly what you would expect if `goog.inherits` got marked as referenced through this extra dependency
- the internal error `"Unexpected variable goog"` is consistent with `NameAnalyzer`/removal logic keeping a malformed leftover reference structure around the `goog.inherits` call

So the likely root cause is:
- `FindReferences.visit(...)` incorrectly treats the inheritance helper function (`goog.inherits`) as a regular dependency target of the subclass
- this can keep the call alive even when the subclass should be removed entirely
